items.body:
## Summary

Existing ChatGPT conversations intermittently fail to load in the Windows desktop app (Windows package `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0`). The user has experienced this twice. During the failure the same conversations remain accessible in the mobile app over LTE. On the latest occurrence, sending a prompt from mobile was followed by recovery of conversation loading on desktop.

This mobile-to-desktop recovery pattern is observed, not a proven causal mechanism. Mobile changes both client and network, so the evidence does not isolate client state, request-specific backend handling, or routing differences.

## Latest occurrence

2026-10-21, around **11:12 KST / 02:12 UTC**. A separate earlier 09:xx local network problem is explicitly out of scope.

There were **13 logged failed requests between 02:04:44 and 02:17:08 UTC** with `status=500` and a specific response body:

```json
{"detail":"Can't load conversation [redacted]"}
```

These are request failures, not 13 separate outages:
- Conversation A: 7 failures across initialization and both conversation-read routes.
- Conversation B: 4 failures across initialization, conversation retrieval and paginated message retrieval.
- Conversation C: named in 2 failures while retrieving `/pins`.

Routes included:
- `POST /conversation/init`
- `GET /conversations/{conversation_id}`
- `GET /conversation/{conversation_id}`
- `GET /conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`
- `GET /pins`

## Timeline and log evidence

All timestamps below are UTC on 2026-10-21. IDs and local paths are redacted.

```text
02:00:13.251 chatgpt_conversation_refetch_completed conversationId=[A]
             currentNodeApplied=true statusAfter=idle
02:04:44.748 sa_server_request_failed method=post
             routePattern=/conversation/init status=500
             errorMessage={"detail":"Can't load conversation [A]"}
02:12:36.860 sa_server_request_failed method=post
             routePattern=/conversation/init status=500
             errorMessage={"detail":"Can't load conversation [A]"}
02:23:39.673 chatgpt_conversation_refetch_completed conversationId=[A]
             currentNodeApplied=false statusBefore=error statusAfter=error
02:28:24.409 chatgpt_conversation_refetch_completed conversationId=[A]
             currentNodeApplied=false statusAfter=error
02:28:29.111 chatgpt_conversation_refetch_completed conversationId=[A]
             currentNodeApplied=false statusAfter=error
```

The lines above are abbreviated extracts, not verbatim complete log lines. The completed refetches retained an error state. We cannot establish from these fields alone whether this is a UI recovery defect or retained conversation execution state.

## Observed reproduction / recovery sequence

1. Open an existing conversation on Windows desktop.
2. Conversation loading fails.
3. Open the same conversation in the mobile app over LTE: it works.
4. Submit a prompt from mobile.
5. Desktop conversation loading subsequently recovers.

The user reports two occurrences of the desktop/mobile discrepancy. The latest prompt/recovery sequence was reported by the user; its exact send/recovery timestamps were not captured independently.

## Local checks

- Installed Windows package: `OpenAI.Codex 26.1013.4894.0`.
- Read-only `PRAGMA quick_check` passed for `state_5.sqlite`, `thread_history_1.sqlite` and `logs_2.sqlite`. These checks do not verify cloud conversation storage.
- No contemporaneous ChatGPT/Codex application crash or hang event was found in Windows event logs.
- Subsequent read-only `read_thread` calls returned one recent turn for all three affected conversations. This does not prove complete historical integrity or that the UI had recovered at the time of those reads.
- Relevant raw desktop logs were preserved locally with SHA-256 hashes.

## Requested investigation

Please correlate conversation initialization, paginated reads and pins failures, and inspect desktop recovery after a refetch succeeds. In particular:
- Can a new mobile message change shared conversation state or emit an update that unblocks the desktop?
- Does desktop initialization/pagination use a different path from mobile?
- Why does the logged error state persist after completed refetches?

OpenAI Help Center's AI-assisted support mentioned an active incident affecting Conversations and Codex in ChatGPT Desktop, but did not establish that this recurrence shares that incident's cause. It could not provide a case number or human handoff and suggested in-app feedback or this issue tracker.

Private conversation identifiers, titles, email, credentials, message content and local paths are intentionally omitted from this public issue. Conversation identifiers and fuller extracted evidence can be supplied through an appropriate private OpenAI support channel if needed.

items.title: [macOS Desktop] @ browser discovery self-probes trigger untrusted-process-ancestry warnings

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1013.40934 (build 20770), production channel; desktop app installed as ChatGPT.app, bundle identifier com.openai.codex.

### What subscription do you have?

Omitted for privacy; this report concerns local browser discovery and native process validation.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon / arm64. Chrome 155.0.8059.85.

### What issue are you seeing?

Opening the @ browser/app picker repeatedly produces native-pipe trust-rejection warnings even when browser discovery is functioning. A focused diagnostic identified the desktop main process itself as the discovery client.

Sanitized message (timestamps and all local identifiers omitted):
```text
[browser-use-native-pipe-server] browser-use native pipe rejected socket peer reason=untrusted-process-ancestry
```

Read-only inspection of the installed app indicates that the Chrome-tab mention discovery scans same-user sockets in a shared native-browser discovery directory, connects to candidates, and only then checks getInfo to determine whether a candidate is a Chrome extension. That directory also contains in-process IAB / MCP Apps endpoints.

The native authorizer checks whether the connecting process descends from the server process before checking signing identity. A process is not its own descendant, so the app probing its own endpoint produces the same ancestry-rejection reason. This appears to be an interaction between endpoint discovery and the ancestry rule, rather than evidence that the browser connector signature is damaged.

Scope: this report establishes the self-probe warning path. It does not establish that all intermittent missing-browser or disconnected-browser symptoms have this cause. Normal browser inventory succeeded during and after this investigation.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start the macOS desktop app with the Chrome integration available and a normal local chat with built-in browser backends initialized.
2. Type @ in the chat input to open the app/browser picker; no message needs to be sent.
3. Observe the desktop native-pipe logs. Close and reopen the picker to repeat the scan.
4. Compare the discovery client process with the desktop main process. In the observed run, a temporary same-user, owner-only diagnostic listener recorded the peer PID through macOS LOCAL_PEERPID during two picker scans. In both cases it mapped to the desktop main process; the matching rejection messages appeared in the same scan windows. The observer recorded only process attribution, did not collect page content, and was removed afterward.

Isolated control using the original, unmodified browser-use-peer-authorization.node and the app-bundled signed Node runtime:
```js
const authorizer = require(process.env.AUTH_ADDON);
// In an independent test server connection handler:
const result = authorizer.authorizeSocketPeer(socket._handle.fd, false);
```

| Connecting process | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same signed Node process connecting to its own test listener | authorized: false; untrusted-process-ancestry |
| Signed Node child connecting to the parent test listener | authorized: true; signingIdentifier: node |
| System/Homebrew Node child (control) | authorized: false; missing-code-signing-identity |

The test listeners were separate from the application endpoints and were cleaned up. The existing validator was not changed or bypassed.

### What is the expected behavior?

Opening the @ picker should discover supported browser providers without probing the app’s own protected endpoints as if they were external Chrome providers and emitting misleading trust-rejection warnings.

Please distinguish expected discovery filtering from actual failed browser connections. If in-process self-connections are intentional, handle that narrow case deliberately while preserving signing checks, descendant-process restrictions for other clients, browser permissions, and chat isolation. Suggested regression cases: same-process discovery, trusted child client, unrelated same-user client, and unrelated native-browser endpoint.

### Additional information

Related: #54720 reports a separate shared-server topology with the same rejection reason. This report is specifically about desktop-main-process self-probes during @ picker discovery; a common root cause with shared-server or remote failures has not been established.

The desktop app and bundled Chrome native host both passed signature verification outside the agent sandbox. Signature checking inside the restricted sandbox initially gave misleading failures, so those results were not treated as proof of corruption. The app updater reported no available production update at investigation time.

No app code, native authorizer, browser manifest, or trust policy was modified. No browser security controls were disabled. Unrelated local installation anomalies are intentionally excluded.

Privacy: no account/subscription details, usernames, home paths, hostnames, process IDs, socket names, chat/session IDs, browsing history, website titles/URLs, full logs, or diagnostic attachments are included. Only the generic error text, product versions, reproduction procedure, and summarized control results are published.

items.title: Retained images exceed Responses WebSocket size limit: five retries before HTTP fallback; 16 MiB ± 1 byte reproduction

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Desktop bundle: `26.1013.40934`, build `20770` (read from the installed app's Info.plist).
Installed bundled CLI reports `0.163.0-alpha.10.2`. The already-running process was not restarted or binary-matched during diagnosis, so this does not establish its exact build.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro, using ChatGPT sign-in.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon (arm64).

### What issue are you seeing?

An existing image-heavy conversation repeatedly displayed:

```text
Reconnecting 5/5
stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
```

Each WebSocket handshake succeeded, but the client retried the full request five times before falling back to HTTP. HTTP then succeeded and the conversation resumed.

This is related to #55317 and #38846. This report adds an independent, minimal **JSON-whitespace boundary control at 16 MiB ± 1 byte**, and focuses on byte-aware preflight/fallback and loss of Close-code diagnostics. It does not reproduce or claim the heartbeat timeout discussed in #55317.

#### Original incident evidence

On 2026-10-21 (UTC+08:00):

- 10:07:29: WebSocket connected successfully.
- 10:07:43–10:08:02: retries 1/5 through 5/5, each with the error above.
- Reconnection logs contain `non-incremental request reason="connection_closed"`.
- 10:08:08: `falling back to HTTP`.
- The subsequent HTTP request log records `pre_compression_bytes=19094865 post_compression_bytes=11130448` using zstd.
- 10:08:15: HTTP 200; assistant output and tool execution subsequently resumed.

The HTTP body's uncompressed size is **19,094,865 bytes (18.21 MiB)**. This is a measured HTTP fallback body, not a captured byte-for-byte copy of the failed WebSocket message.

A read-only reconstruction using the last `compacted.replacement_history` plus subsequent `response_item` records, up to the turn's start, found:

- 152 history items.
- **9 retained inline user images: 18,189,822 data-URL bytes (17.35 MiB)**.
- Serialized reconstructed history: 18,972,342 bytes, before additional runtime instructions/tool schemas and any runtime filtering.
- The most recent recorded compaction had retained historical images; the images alone exceeded the boundary measured below.

The historical failure's Close code was not preserved. Therefore, attributing that original incident to size rejection is a strongly supported inference, **not a claim that its actual Close frame was captured as 1009**.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

#### Controlled transport test (completed)

Using a separate Python standard-library WebSocket probe, connect to the same authenticated Responses endpoint, `wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`, through the existing local HTTP CONNECT proxy.

Serialize this synthetic warmup event as compact UTF-8 JSON:

```json
{"type":"response.create","model":"gpt-6-astra","instructions":"Diagnostic warmup.","input":[],"tools":[],"store":false,"generate":false}
```

For each target size, append ASCII spaces **after the closing JSON brace**, so the message remains valid JSON with identical semantic content:

```python
payload = json.dumps(event, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
payload += b" " * (target_bytes - len(payload))
assert len(payload) == target_bytes
```

Use a fresh WebSocket connection per case. Send one logical Text message in 64 KiB continuation fragments, with FIN only on the last fragment. Mask client frames and respond to server Ping frames. Do not negotiate permessage-deflate. Read the raw server Close frame as well as response events.

| Exact logical message bytes | Upgrade | Result | Total elapsed |
| ---: | --- | --- | ---: |
| 1,024 | HTTP 101 | `response.completed` | 3.32 s |
| **16,777,215 (16 MiB − 1)** | HTTP 101 | **`response.completed`** | 6.68 s |
| **16,777,217 (16 MiB + 1)** | HTTP 101 | **Received Close 1009, empty reason**; no response events | 7.11 s |

All three cases used the same endpoint, account, model, proxy and selected upstream node. Only the trailing whitespace byte count changed. No original images, prompts or conversation history were transmitted by the probes. `generate=false` produced no model output.

This brackets a size-sensitive rejection within two bytes around 16 MiB on this route. It does not establish the exact inclusive configured limit, which backend/edge component enforces it, or limits for other endpoints. Fragmentation does not bypass the logical-message limit.

#### Network context

Clash uses mixed port 7897. The desktop and backend processes inherited HTTP/HTTPS proxy variables plus a SOCKS5 ALL_PROXY value. Matching local socket ports against the Clash connection table confirmed active backend connections to chatgpt.com using HTTP CONNECT. The synthetic probes explicitly used that same HTTP CONNECT proxy without changing network configuration.

Below-boundary success and above-boundary Close 1009 on the same route give a more specific explanation than a general proxy outage. They do not prove that every reconnect error has this cause.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Consider a serialized-byte budget separately from token/context limits, including retained inline image data.
- When the request is known to exceed the supported WebSocket budget, select a supported transport or recovery path before repeatedly uploading it.
- Preserve Close code/reason and classify a received 1009 as non-transient for an unchanged payload; avoid retrying the same oversized request five times.
- Provide an actionable error and a supported way to recover an affected conversation without losing useful context.

HTTP fallback already recovered this incident. The issue is the avoidable retry loop and misleading generic network diagnosis.

### Additional information

The public source's `Message::Close(_)` branch returns a generic error without including the code/reason:
https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4ebc485ca321243727539187169425fcf972f2c4/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs#L945

The probe uses the documented warmup behavior:
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/websocket-mode

No original screenshots, private prompts, raw rollouts, account/thread/turn identifiers, credentials, personal filesystem paths or proxy server addresses are included in this report. Original history and application/network settings were not modified.
